title: Breast Augmentation Pain: Timeline, Ibuprofen, Nerve Pain
meta_description: Acute pain usually eases in 1 to 5 days, ASPS says. A pain timeline, whether you can take ibuprofen, why nerve zaps happen, and the pain that needs a call.
excerpt: Pain after breast augmentation peaks in the first days and eases over the first week or so, with soreness lingering a few weeks and nerve zaps coming and going for months. Here is the timeline, what the evidence says about ibuprofen and gabapentin, what helps at home, and when pain is not normal. No doses, on purpose.
quick_answer:
How long does pain last after breast augmentation?

Acute pain typically eases after 1 to 5 days, ASPS says, though soreness and swelling can last a few weeks. The Aesthetic Society says the first 48 hours are usually worst and that implants under the muscle hurt more. University of Utah Health says shooting pains can last a few months. Take only what your surgeon approves.

sources.title: What should I expect during my breast augmentation recovery?
quotes: Acute pain typically subsides after one to five days, but you may experience soreness and swelling for a few weeks.
Wear your support garment (a bra or elastic band, called a bandeau) around the clock as instructed by your plastic surgeon.

sources.title: Breast Augmentation - Aftercare & Recovery
quotes: Breast augmentation surgery stretches the breast tissue and it can be painful—especially when your implants are underneath the pectoral muscle.
Typically, you’ll experience the most pain within the first 48 hours after surgery.
Your pain level will typically decrease each day
If the pain is extreme or long-lasting, contact your surgeon.
Your chest area may feel stiff and sore for two to five days.

Rest and sleep on your back in an inclined position (25-to 45-degree angle) for the initial postoperative days or if you have significant swelling. Use wedge pillows with an incline design or sleep in a recliner chair.
It is very important that you walk a few minutes every few hours to reduce the risk of blood clot formation in your legs.
Your breasts may feel tight and sensitive to the touch and your skin may feel warm or itchy.

sources.publisher: UW Medicine, University of Washington Medical Center
sources.title: Breast Augmentation: What to expect and how to prepare (handout PDF)
quotes: The first 12 to 24 hours after surgery are usually the most painful.
It is normal to have muscle soreness or sharp, shooting pain for 2 weeks after surgery.
You will be given a prescription for pain medicine. Take this medicine exactly as it was prescribed.
For the first 2 to 3 days, you may use ice packs over your whole breast area to lessen swelling, pain, and bruising.
Wrap the ice packs in a towel or cloth to protect your skin.
Apply the ice packs for 20 minutes each hour.
If doing something hurts or pulls on your incisions, stop what you are doing.
Severe pain that is not helped by your pain medicine
A fever higher than 100.5°F (38°C)

sources.title: Recovering from Breast Reduction & Breast Augmentation
quotes: You may feel shooting pains, tingling, or other strange sensations in your skin for the first few months.
You may experience some asymmetry since each breast may heal at a different rate.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, article by Ariel Frankeny, freelance writer
sources.title: Back to active: Returning to exercise after breast augmentation recovery
quotes: Typically, the first week is the most uncomfortable
especially if the implant was placed under the muscle.
If you have a subpectoral (under the muscle) implant, you'll likely feel some pain, because the muscle has been stretched to accommodate the implant.

sources.title: Cosmetic breast surgery - discharge
quotes: Do not take aspirin, aspirin-containing medicines, or ibuprofen without your surgeon's approval.
Take them with food and plenty of water. Do not apply ice or heat to your breasts unless your surgeon tells you that it is OK.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking pain medicines.
Smoking slows healing and increases your risk for complications and infection.
A fever of 100°F (38°C) or higher
Increasing pain, redness, swelling, yellow or green drainage, bleeding, or bruising at the incision site
Also contact your surgeon if you notice sudden swelling of your breast.

sources.title: Breast Augmentation
quotes: Pain medication prescribed by your surgeon and/or acetaminophen (Tylenol®).
Avoid taking aspirin and certain anti-inflammatory drugs, since they can increase bleeding.
Increasing enlargement, or firmness, of one or both of your breasts that’s associated with pain and pressure.

sources.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
quotes: Symptoms of this include chest pain, shortness of breath, cough with blood, lightheadedness and fainting.

sources.title: Risks and Complications of Breast Implants
quotes: Capsular contracture is the hardening of the breast around the implant. It can occur in the tissue surrounding one or both implants. This hardening causes the tissue to tighten, which can be painful.

sources.title: Things to Consider Before Getting Breast Implants
quotes: If you notice any abnormal changes in your breasts or implants, you will need to see your surgeon or health care provider promptly.

sources.publisher: Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery (Kelley and colleagues)
sources.title: Ibuprofen May Not Increase Bleeding Risk in Plastic Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
quotes: Four primary randomized controlled trials were selected for full analysis.
No significant difference was noted regarding bleeding events (p = 0.32), and pain control was noted to be equivalent.
This meta-analysis represents a small set of high-quality studies suggesting that ibuprofen provides pain control equivalent to narcotics.
Further large studies will be necessary to elucidate this issue further

sources.title: Ibuprofen doesn't increase bleeding risk after plastic surgery
quotes: But available evidence suggests that ibuprofen does not increase the risk of bleeding after plastic surgery procedures

sources.title: American Society of Plastic Surgeons Member Post-Operative Opioid Prescribing Patterns
quotes: Overall, 80% (N = 240) of respondents used nonnarcotic adjuncts to manage postoperative pain
Of the 5,770 overall active ASPS members, 298 responses (12% response rate) were received
Respondents were randomized to 1 of 3 different common elective procedures in plastic surgery: breast augmentation, breast reduction, and abdominoplasty.
The most commonly prescribed narcotics were Hydrocodone with Acetaminophen (Lortab, Norco) and Oxycodone with Acetaminophen (Percocet, Oxycocet)

sources.title: Pectoral Nerve Blocks for Breast Augmentation Surgery: A Randomized, Double-blind, Dual-centered Controlled Trial
quotes: Seventy-three adult female patients undergoing aesthetic breast augmentation surgery under general anesthesia were randomly allocated to receive a pectoral nerve block versus no block.

Pectoral nerve block in conjunction with multimodal analgesia provides effective perioperative pain relief after aesthetic breast surgery and is associated with reduced opioid consumption over the first 5 postoperative days.

sources.title: Chronic Pain Following Cosmetic Breast Surgery: A Comprehensive Review
quotes: Postoperative chronic pain, defined as lasting 3 or more months, has been reported in a wide variety of breast surgical procedures including breast augmentation, reduction mammaplasty, mastectomy, and mastectomy with reconstruction.

sources.publisher: Pain and Therapy (Urits and colleagues), full text
sources.title: Chronic Pain Following Cosmetic Breast Surgery: A Comprehensive Review (2020)
quotes: Often, medical management provides an avenue to remain comfortable through utilization of over-the-counter analgesics, neuropathic agents, or physical therapy. For some, conservative management is insufficient; strategies may be employed to include regional anesthesia and nerve blocks.
In these patients, medications such as gabapentin or pregabalin may provide some relief
there is conflicting evidence as to the actual efficacy of either of these drugs
These medications are also associated with increased risk of bleeding and should be used with caution in older patients or those prone to bleeding.
Opioids are effective and often used for acute perioperative pain management in breast surgery
However, with the risk for opioid dependence, especially with chronic use, these medications should be limited in patients undergoing breast augmentation

quotes: Ninety-five patients (66.9%) returned the questionnaire

sources.title: Combined preoperative use of celecoxib and gabapentin in the management of postoperative pain
quotes: Gabapentin (Neurontin) is an agent commonly used to control neuropathic pain.

Here we describe a prospective study assessing the efficacy of preoperative gabapentin in combination with celecoxib for reducing postoperative pain and opioid requirements in elective subpectoral breast augmentation.
Results were then compared with those of our previous study in which only celecoxib was used.
